absent: Provider internal scheduling, queueing and hardware programming behind preparation, issue and status operations.
Channel lifetime, reference counting, and concurrency rules beyond safe preparation locking.
DMA address mapping, cache maintenance, residue accuracy, and completion ordering guarantees.
Remapping unit runtime behaviour, table management, and fault handling.
Error recovery, timeout, pause resume interaction with termination, and cancellation ordering.
Perf, printk, power, module, audit and debug interactions implied by the dossier title but not shown here.

findings.text: Provider record keeps lifetime and topology state using a reference count, total and private channel counts, owned channel list and global linkage, selection filter, capability mask, descriptor metadata modes, xor and parity source limits, four alignment needs for copy xor parity and fill, numeric identity, backing device pointer, owner module, and channel identifier allocator. It also stores peripheral capability data for address widths, directions, burst sizes, reuse support, and residue granularity.

Same provider record exposes a driver supplied operation table covering channel resource allocation and release with optional router setup, many preparation operations for copy xor parity memset interrupt vector scatter gather configured scatter gather cyclic and interleaved transfers, capability query and peripheral configuration, pause resume terminate and synchronise controls, status query, pending issue trigger, release hook, plus optional debug summary callback and debug filesystem root.
Small remapping scope record binds one endpoint to its unit with a protected device pointer, a bus number, and a combined device function identifier.

Parity continuation support is encoded as a flag in bit position fifteen inside the stored maximum parity source count. Helpers set the count with or without that flag, test for its presence, and mask it away to yield the plain count.

Remapping header defines an include guard, a maximum unit count of 1024, and four option bits with decimal values 1, 2, 4 and 8 for interrupt remapping, extended APIC opt out, platform opt in, and remapping opt out.

Peripheral configuration wrapper delegates to the provider configuration operation when present and otherwise reports unsupported operation. Direction predicate is true exactly for memory to device, device to memory, and device to device transfers, and false for all other directions.

Single buffer and scatter list preparation helpers share one fallback chain. They reject absent channel or provider, prefer a combined provider configure plus prepare operation when available, otherwise apply separate peripheral configuration when supplied and then use plain scatter gather preparation, failing when needed operations are missing or configuration fails. Single buffer forms build an internal one element scatter description, and null configuration forms forward to configured forms.

Safe configured preparation wrappers hold the channel interrupt saving spin lock across the fallback preparation path only when the provider lacks a combined configure plus prepare operation, then release it and return the prepared transaction. Single buffer safe form builds a one element scatter description and forwards to the scatter safe form.

Vector, RapidIO, cyclic and interleaved preparation helpers validate channel, provider and the matching provider operation and return an absent marker when any is missing, otherwise forward their arguments. The interleaved helper additionally rejects repeat requests when the provider capability mask does not advertise repeat support.

Memory set and copy preparation helpers guard on channel, provider and the matching provider operation before delegation. Metadata mode query reports false for an absent channel and otherwise tests whether the requested mode bits appear in the provider supported modes.

In this configuration descriptor metadata helpers are unsupported placeholders. Attach and length establishment always report invalid argument and pointer query always returns an absent marker without changing the descriptor.

Channel control wrappers delegate pause, resume and termination to provider operations when present and otherwise report unsupported operation, except one asynchronous termination variant reports invalid argument when missing. Synchronisation allows sleeping and calls provider synchronisation only when present. Synchronous termination first tries asynchronous termination and on success waits for synchronisation before reporting success.

Status query forwards cookie and state storage to the provider status operation. Submission invokes the descriptor stored submit callback. Alignment checking verifies that two offsets and a length are multiples of a power of two derived from an alignment level, with conveniences applying it to provider copy, xor, parity and fill requirements.

Continuation predicates test flag combinations for plain continuation and for continuation with parity disabled. Maximum parity source computation returns the plain maximum when continuation is supported or not requested, reduces it by one for disabled parity continuation and by three for other continuation, with an unreachable trap otherwise. Gap helpers choose direction specific, generic, or zero gap from increment and scatter settings.

Engine reference helpers are empty no operation placeholders in every observed variant, as are asynchronous engine get and put aliases. Channel lookup aliases either always return an absent marker, forward to a generic asynchronous transaction lookup, or map the requested type directly, depending on configuration.

Transaction acknowledgement helpers set, clear and test an acknowledgement flag inside descriptor flags. Capability mask helpers set, clear, zero and test individual transaction type bits and iterate over set bits up to a defined terminator, with short aliases forwarding to the underlying implementations.

Pending issue trigger forwards directly to the provider issue operation. Transaction completion query forwards to provider status and copies last completed and last used cookies to optional outputs. Cookie comparison implements a wrap aware completion test for normal and wrapped counter ranges. State initialiser stores last, used and residue values unless state storage is absent.

In this configuration channel discovery and management are fallback stubs. Lookup and low level request always return an absent marker, named and masked requests always report missing device, release and global issue are empty, synchronous waits always report completion, and slave capability query always reports unavailable device. Mask macro forwards to low level request, named slave request maps errors to absent marker, and compatibility helper tries named request first then filtered mask request when filter arguments exist.

Reusable descriptor helpers manage a reuse flag. Establishment queries slave capabilities and only sets the flag when reuse is advertised, otherwise reporting query or permission failure. Clearing removes the flag, testing reports it, and freeing rejects non reusable descriptors and otherwise invokes the descriptor owned free callback.

Direction naming maps device to memory, memory to device, memory to memory, and device to device to DEV_TO_MEM, MEM_TO_DEV, MEM_TO_MEM, and DEV_TO_DEV, with any other value mapped to invalid. Owning device lookup returns the channel private DMA device when present and otherwise the provider device pointer.

Normal channel use moves from preparation yielding a transaction descriptor, through optional acknowledgement or reuse marking, submission through the stored callback, issue of pending work, completion polling by cookie with last and used markers, and termination plus synchronisation. Pause and resume may interpose while active, and peripheral configuration may precede preparation.

Many wrappers only check for absent channel, provider or operation before dispatch, so callers must stabilise channel lifetime. Missing control operations fail rather than succeeding silently. Synchronisation may sleep and is unsuitable for atomic context. Maximum parity logic has an unreachable trap for unexpected flag combinations. Safe preparation locking covers only the fallback path without combined provider support.

Driver facing entry surface is the provider operation table in the device record plus inline wrappers for preparation, submission, status and control that validate arguments and dispatch to it. Channel acquisition, release and capability query complete the entry surface in fuller configurations.
